code_paths.purpose: Handles the 'ledger_closed' RPC command, retrieves the most recently closed ledger, validates its existence, and returns its index and hash.

transformations: ledger->header().hash converted to string via to_string

description: Provides the implementation of the doLedgerClosed function, which returns information about the most recently closed ledger in JSON format.

false_positive_patterns.issue_pattern: Missing empty string validation for ledger (closed ledger pointer)
false_positive_patterns.why_false_positive: XRPL_ASSERT validates ledger (closed ledger pointer) for empty strings
JSON String constants - indicates template validation

namespace_accessors.audit_implication: Fields accessed via this namespace are framework-validated
namespace_accessors.meaning: JSON String constants - indicates template validation

test_coverage_notes: This handler is typically tested via RPC integration tests that call the 'ledger_closed' method and check the returned ledger_index and ledger_hash. Likely test files: rpc/ledger_closed_test.cpp, rpc/LedgerHandler_test.cpp, or similar. Unit tests for LedgerMaster::getClosedLedger may exist. Gaps: No explicit test for XRPL_ASSERT failure (i.e., if getClosedLedger returns null), as this is an invariant violation and would typically crash or abort in debug builds. No direct test for malformed or missing context, as context is constructed by the RPC framework.

validation_architecture.framework: XRPL_ASSERT (custom assertion macro), jss:: (field naming, not validation)
validation_architecture.notes: No input or field validation is performed on user-supplied data in this handler. The only validation is an internal assertion that the closed ledger pointer is non-null. jss:: is used for JSON field naming, not validation. No template, type, range, or format validation is present in this code.

validations.error_thrown: assertion failure (likely aborts or throws in debug)
validates: closed ledger must exist before proceeding
